Multi-Tier Model Benchmark Bar Charts

Source: R/type_benchmark_bars.R
type_benchmark_bars.Rd

Creates publication-quality tiered model benchmark bar charts with grouped-jackknife / bootstrap confidence intervals, print-safe borders, and permutation null distribution reference bands. Designed for rigorous multi-omics drug target prioritization and machine learning benchmarks (multiomics_paper / Liu et al.).

Usage

type_benchmark_bars(
  null_band = NULL,
  value_labels = TRUE,
  error_low = NULL,
  error_high = NULL,
  bar_width = 0.75,
  cap_size = 0.25,
  border_color = "black",
  border_width = 0.5,
  label_format = "%.2f",
  text_size = 3,
  group_sep_lines = NULL,
  log_scale = FALSE,
  ...
)

type_benchmark(...)

Arguments

null_band

Numeric vector of length 2 giving the lower and upper bounds of the permutation null distribution (e.g., c(0.505, 0.549)), drawn as a neutral reference band behind the bars.

value_labels

Logical. Whether to print exact performance values above the error whiskers (default TRUE).

error_low

Column name or vector for lower confidence interval bounds.

error_high

Column name or vector for upper confidence interval bounds.

bar_width

Bar width (default 0.75).

cap_size

Error bar whisker cap size (default 0.25).

border_color

Bar border color (default "black").

border_width

Bar border line width (default 0.5).

label_format

Character format string for annotations (default "\%.2f").

text_size

Numeric text size for annotations (default 3.0).

group_sep_lines

Vector of x-axis positions or category names where vertical dotted boundary lines should be drawn between governance tiers (default NULL).

log_scale

Logical. Whether y-axis should be log10 transformed (useful for AP lift; default FALSE).

...

Additional arguments.

Value

A cliplot_type object for use with cliplot.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
df_bench = data.frame(
  model     = c("Biology", "Druggability", "B+D", "Attention", "Clinical", "Label"),
  auroc     = c(0.77, 0.77, 0.86, 0.91, 0.89, 0.98),
  auroc_lo  = c(0.69, 0.68, 0.78, 0.84, 0.82, 0.94),
  auroc_hi  = c(0.85, 0.84, 0.92, 0.97, 0.96, 1.00),
  learner   = rep("HGB", 6)
)
cliplot(auroc ~ model, data = df_bench,
        type = type_benchmark_bars(null_band = c(0.505, 0.549)))
} # }
